# HoBo

> HoBo is an AI-native meta-cloud, currently pre-release, with one guiding principle:
> every app deserves a home — preferably a cheap one. You describe an app once as a
> provider-agnostic "Bindle"; HoBo places it in a "Camp" (one provider + a durable
> runtime) that passes your policies, and then CONTINUOUS MIGRATION keeps re-deciding
> placement for as long as the app lives — moving it when a cheaper valid home opens up.
> The programmable surface is WIT/WASM (Component Model / wasmCloud); TypeScript is the
> first reference implementation. Agents are first-class principals with scoped
> short-lived credentials, an MCP control surface with full capability parity, and a
> replayable event log for every action.

Key facts:

- Guiding principle: placement is a standing decision. The Dispatcher continuously re-plans
  where the app lives, optimizing cost under policy; migrations run the same plan → gate →
  converge loop as deploys, so a move is never a special event.
- Primitives, in order of need: Bindle (the one REQUIRED authoring primitive — the packed,
  provider-agnostic app) → Camp (its current home: one provider + durable runtime; every
  app lives in one, but WRITING one is optional — unspecified camps are inferred from the
  configured code, unless a junction broker admin locks placement down to explicit camps) →
  Yard (advanced — one provider's camps: shared policy/identity) → Junction (advanced —
  cross-cloud federation of yards, peer-to-peer, no shared mutable state; junction
  governance is where camp inference can be disabled).
- One lifecycle verb pair: `hobo up` realizes the object graph (build, plan, gate,
  provision, deploy); `hobo down` reverses it. `hobo dev` runs an offline local camp;
  `npx hobo new` scaffolds; anonymous `npx hobo up` deploys with no account, `hobo claim`
  binds it later.
- Everything is event-sourced and replayable, including agent token issuance and every
  migration decision.
- The Conductor (branded name; technically "the broker", @hobo/broker) is the
  policy-governed decision authority: it brokers bindle/camp/yard/junction placements
  PER RESOURCE across providers under the configured policy set it maintains, answers
  with a content-hash-pinned, Ed25519-signable Resolution Receipt or a per-plane
  Resolution Rejection from a closed rejection catalog with remediations, handles spin
  up/down/zero, and wraps five swappable planes — policy (typed TS policy packs by
  default, real OPA/Rego decisions at hobo/broker/decision with fail-closed semantics,
  Cedar planned), contracts (Gatekeeper/PACT can-deploy), billing (budget/spend-cap/
  quota, plus a metered plane folding meter.UsageRecorded facts), delivery (Argo CD
  Application rendering plus live fail-closed Argo CD API submission), and a connector
  registry (github-app, pulumi, azure, vercel, cloudflare; credentialRef pointers only,
  never secrets). Junction broker-admin lockdowns accumulate and cannot be relaxed by
  narrower policies. On the CLI: `hobo broker config [--init]` scaffolds/validates
  hobo.broker.json (policies, budgets, connectors, OPA/Cedar policyEngine, delivery);
  `hobo broker up` realizes placements — with NO cloud config, the running machine
  registers itself as a zero-cost local HoBo provider host so the whole loop is
  testable on a bare machine.
- Providers, IaC engines, and build tools sit behind WIT ports with conformance-gated
  adapters — AI-generated adapters are certified by the same contract suites as
  human-written ones.
- Bindles support brownfield AND greenfield. A component is declared as a `@component`
  class whose `@operation` methods (TC39 stage-3 decorators from @hobo/runtime) carry
  { intent, contract with a REQUIRED typed input/output shape (+ invariants, forbidden
  outputs, examples), OPTIONAL rubric (scorer → promotion threshold, enforced as policy;
  absent → default exact-match over examples/traces) }; per-parameter metadata uses
  param(). An operation whose body is stub() — or a bare field — declares CODE TO BE
  GENERATED; a hand-written body is the baseline. b.api/b.web/b.service accept the
  decorated class directly. Operations lower to trainables (signature-only when stubbed);
  contract-derived stubs serve the app end-to-end on day one, stub calls record
  specification-by-example traces, and the generation pipeline synthesizes real WIT
  component implementations — promoted only when conformance passes, eval thresholds are
  met, and policy allows. Escalation is per-operation: stub → `"use training"` body
  (AI-maintained) → plain hand-maintained body, with no manifest change. Granular
  alternative — ALL decorators optional: @intent/@returns on methods, @description on
  parameters (a real parameter decorator in legacy-decorator projects; a params: map
  value under standard decorators), bare @trainable composing the class; missing
  groundings are inferred. Ambient `@trainable export declare class` declarations (pure
  signatures, no bodies) are scanned statically by `hobo stub`, which takes the
  TypeScript signature as the declared shape and generates grounded training.define
  registrations.
- Status: pre-release, with a real shipped slice. The TypeScript authoring flow runs
  today: a project's `src/bindle.ts` (default export of `bindle()` from @hobo/bindles)
  drives `hobo collect` / `hobo plan` / `hobo up` / `hobo dev` against the default
  LOCAL lane (`hobo dev` serves the project's own api/web handler in-process; a
  committed `hobo.bindle.json` artifact wins when present). Durable Camp EventStore
  defaults to a single-owner SQLite partition (@hobo/storage-sqlite +
  @hobo/runtime-local): stream-head CAS, actor fencing, positioned catch-up, atomic
  domain events + staged queue/timer/outbox; browser OPFS path via
  @hobo/runtime-browser (fail-closed without OPFS when durable is required). SQLite
  is the default engine behind ports, not the public portability boundary — scale by
  partitions, never multi-writer shared WAL. BoundaryContracts may declare EffectSpec
  (purity + domain I/O) and secondary ResilienceProfile metadata; effect widening can
  break can-deploy; never retry policy.Decided deny or terminal failures
  (@hobo/contracts, @hobo/contract-harness). No public Effect-TS/Polly/XState deps.
  The `hobo-mcp` binary serves all 28 canonical verbs (including `hobo broker`) as
  MCP tools over stdio with verb/tool parity contract-tested, deny-by-default audited
  auth, and HOBO_MCP_TOOLS scoping. Live deploy lanes are credential-gated
  (Cloudflare/Vercel env tokens; HOBO_PULUMI_LIVE=1 for the real pinned Pulumi engine).
  Session Replay (@hobo/replay, ADR-0137) is shipped locally with dual fixtures.
  Messaging plane (ADR-0138): unified wasi:messaging / topic() port; @hobo/provider-kafka
  (honest live transport harness); optional @hobo/runtime-dapr Camp runtime (actors +
  pubsub; secretless component YAML); hobo messaging + doctor readiness; conformance
  against Kafka and Dapr adapters. In-process wasm remains default (ADR-0031). Not yet
  shipped: full multi-cloud provider adapters; @hobo/junctions maturity (deferred to the
  S4 multi-cloud stage) and the fly/aws/azure/gcp provider and postgres runtime packages —
  the docs mark those pages design-stage. Everything else documented on the site is the
  contract-pinned surface the product is being built to.
- The complete documentation, concatenated as one markdown document, is at
  https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/llms-full.txt. Every docs page also has a
  "Copy page as Markdown" button and per-snippet copy buttons.
